facts.fact_text: All applicants were members of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan.
All applicants were activists of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan.
The applicants attended unauthorised opposition demonstrations organised by the Ictimai Palata group, held in Baku on 14 May 2012.
The applicants attended unauthorised opposition demonstrations organised by the Ictimai Palata group, held in Baku on 21 May 2012.
According to the applicants, the participants in the demonstration of 14 May 2012 were demanding action against corruption.
According to the applicants, the participants in the demonstration of 14 May 2012 were demanding action against violation of human rights.
According to the applicants, on 21 May 2012 the demonstration participants were reportedly demanding the release of political prisoners detained in Azerbaijan.
The applicants submitted that the demonstrations had been intended to be peaceful.
The applicants submitted that the demonstrations had been conducted in a peaceful manner.
Shortly after the applicants joined the demonstrations, the police started to disperse the protesters.

According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), shortly after the police operation to disperse the demonstration of 14 May 2012 had started, around six or seven police officers pushed her so that she almost fell off a ladder.

According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova) held onto her and prevented her from falling off the ladder during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), a police officer, whom she did not know, slapped her neck during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), after being slapped on the neck she suddenly became unable to control her physical movements.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), after being slapped on the neck her vision had temporarily darkened.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she felt pain in her right shoulder, right ear and eyes for a long time after the events of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she was forcibly put on a bus by the police, together with six or seven other female participants in the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she was released after being driven around in the city for some time following the demonstration of 14 May 2012.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration several police officers swore at her.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration several police officers applied physical force to her, as a result of which she had bruises for several months.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), police officers dragged her by both hands to a car during the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she was in pain and shouted during the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), she was released by the police with the second applicant's (Ms Salimzade's) help during the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), on 14 May 2012 the police pushed her and she fell to the ground, sustaining injuries and pain.
According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), police officers swore at her during the 14 May 2012 demonstration.

According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), police officers intentionally touched some parts of her body to humiliate her as a woman during the 14 May 2012 demonstration, including pressing her breasts.
According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), on 21 May 2012 police officers pushed her towards a ladder and she fell to the ground, sustaining a contusion.
According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), police officers dragged her through the street by her hands during the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), she lost consciousness during the events of 21 May 2012.
The second applicant (Ms Salimzade) submitted that she had to spend two hours in hospital on 21 May 2012.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer hit her in the knee hard.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), during the dispersal of the demonstration of 14 May 2012 a police officer swore at her.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), the police forcibly put her on a bus which was being used to remove people from the demonstration venue of 14 May 2012.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), at the demonstration of 21 May 2012 the same officer who had insulted her on 14 May 2012 insulted her again.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), she was taken by the police to the Sabail District Police Office following the 21 May 2012 demonstration.
According to the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), at the Sabail District Police Office a police officer swore at her.
According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), during the 14 May 2012 demonstration a police officer hit her from behind and pushed her aside.

According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), as she tried to help the second applicant (Ms Salimzade) during the 14 May 2012 demonstration, police officers grabbed her and pushed her towards a car.
According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), when she tried to escape from a police officer during the 14 May 2012 demonstration, the police officer stepped on her foot to stop her.
According to the fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova), during the 21 May 2012 demonstration she was taken to the Sabail District Police Office in order to stop her participation in the demonstration.

According to the Sabail District Court's decision of 23 October 2012, the applicants participated in unauthorised assemblies on 14 and 21 May 2012 and were removed from the venue of the unlawful assembly, by being put on buses, for having violated public order and not obeying the police officers.

The relevant domestic law concerning freedom of assembly and the organisation and holding of public assemblies is summarised in Gafgaz Mammadov v. Azerbaijan (no. 60259/11, §§ 27-30, 15 October 2015).

On various dates the applicants complained to the Sabail district prosecutor's office, requesting that a criminal investigation be instituted into their ill-treatment during the dispersal of the assemblies.

The Sabail district prosecutor's office questioned police officers from the Sabail District Police Office, namely police officers A.R., M.B., and A.J., in respect of the complaints of all of the applicants.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office questioned police officers S.G. and E.M. in respect of the fourth applicant's (Ms Huseynova's) complaint.
All questioned police officers stated that they had not applied physical force to any of the participants at the demonstration, including the applicants, but had warned the participants to disperse.
The applicants were questioned by the Sabail district prosecutor's office and reiterated their complaints regarding ill-treatment by the police.
Apart from the third applicant (Ms Khalilova), all applicants submitted video footage and photographs taken during the demonstrations to the Sabail district prosecutor's office.
A forensic expert was appointed following criminal complaints lodged by the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova) and the second applicant (Ms Salimzade) on 21 May 2012.
The forensic expert examined the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova) on 25 May 2012.
The forensic expert examined the second applicant (Ms Salimzade) on 31 May 2012.
The forensic expert issued a forensic report on 29 May 2012 in respect of the first applicant (Ms Mahaddinova), according to which there were no traces of any injuries on her.
The forensic expert issued a forensic report on 31 May 2012 in respect of the second applicant (Ms Salimzade), according to which there were no traces of any injuries on her.
The third applicant (Ms Khalilova) refused to be examined by the forensic expert, claiming that the signs of ill-treatment had disappeared with the passage of time.
The fourth applicant (Ms Huseynova) refused to be examined by the forensic expert, claiming that the signs of ill-treatment had disappeared with the passage of time.
By a decision of 1 June 2012, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case in respect of the first applicant's (Ms Mahaddinova's) complaint.
By a decision of 1 June 2012, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case in respect of the second applicant's (Ms Salimzade's) complaint.
By a decision of 30 June 2012, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case in respect of the fourth applicant's (Ms Huseynova's) complaint.
By a decision of 6 July 2012, the Sabail district prosecutor's office refused to open a criminal case in respect of the third applicant's (Ms Khalilova's) complaint.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office addressed the applicants' complaints with regard to the demonstration of 14 May 2012 only.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office relied on the police officers' statements in refusing to open criminal cases.
The Sabail district prosecutor's office relied on the lack of proof that the applicants had in fact been injured in refusing to open criminal cases.
On an unspecified date the applicants lodged a criminal complaint with the Sabail District Court against the refusals to open a criminal case.
The applicants complained to the Sabail District Court that the security camera recordings relating to the demonstrations in question had not been reviewed during the investigation.
The applicants complained to the Sabail District Court that the witnesses who had observed the police using force against them had not been called or examined during the investigation.
The applicants complained to the Sabail District Court that the investigation had not had regard to the video footage and photographs of the demonstrations they had submitted.

The applicants complained to the Sabail District Court that the police officers questioned by the Sabail district prosecutor's office had been selected randomly, without regard to the officers' personal involvement in the applicants' cases.

The applicants complained to the Sabail District Court that the Sabail district prosecutor's office had not conducted any investigation into the demonstration of 21 May 2012 despite the applicants' specific complaints in this connection.
On 23 October 2012 the Sabail District Court, examining the case in the framework of the judicial supervision procedure, dismissed the applicants' complaints.
On 23 October 2012 the Sabail District Court found the prosecuting authorities' refusals to open criminal proceedings lawful.
The Sabail District Court held on 23 October 2012 that the applicants' claims of having been subjected to attacks and ill-treatment by the police officers concerned had not been proved.
The Sabail District Court found on 23 October 2012 that there was no criminal offence in the police officers' actions.
The analysis section of the Sabail District Court's decision of 23 October 2012 addressed the parties' submissions concerning the assembly on 14 May 2012 only.
On 5 November 2012 the applicants filed an appeal in which they reiterated their previous complaints.
On 16 November 2012 the Baku Court of Appeal upheld the Sabail District Court's decision of 23 October 2012.
On 16 November 2012 the Baku Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' appeal.
The relevant domestic law concerning the prohibition of ill-treatment is summarised in Mustafa Hajili v. Azerbaijan (no. 42119/12, §§ 26-28, 24 November 2016).
